note: Written by Claude from reputable outlets (Reuters, AP, CNA/Straits Times, CNBC, Japan Times and others); source under each story. Disclosure: Claude is made by Anthropic, which appears in today's news. Sports excluded.

items.headline: Anthropic files publicly for Nasdaq IPO under ticker ANT
items.summary:
The Claude developer made its S-1 public on Monday. It reported about $16.3bn of revenue in the first half of 2026 and an $80.7bn net loss, most of it a $72.4bn non-cash charge on convertible notes; the operating loss was $693m.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead 24 underwriters. Share count and price range are not yet set, and the prospectus devotes a large section to AI risks.

items.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 staff
items.summary: That is more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the company tries to contain costs while funding AI data centres. Microsoft has forecast $175bn of capital spending for 2026 and reports quarterly results after the US close on Wednesday.

items.headline: Nvidia to invest in Meta's giant equity raise
items.summary: Nvidia said it would buy into Meta's share offering, now enlarged to about $97.5bn, as the two expand an AI-agent partnership. Chip stocks rallied on the news and on Anthropic's filing.

items.headline: Super Micro-backed Argentum AI in talks for $5bn chip financing
items.summary: The 'neocloud' operator is negotiating a $5bn deal with a major private-credit firm to fund AI chips, two sources said, a sign of how much AI build-out is now debt-financed.

items.headline: Applied Materials to lift Besi stake to about 20%
items.summary: The US chip-equipment maker will more than double its holding in the Dutch chip-packaging firm from 9%, subject to US antitrust review. It says it has no plan to go above 20% or seek a board seat.

items.headline: Wall Street extends gains as chips rally
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.6% to 7,722.60, about 1.2% below its record. The Nasdaq gained 1.18% to 26,477.81 and the Dow was flat at 52,377.57. The Philadelphia chip index jumped 3.6% for a third straight gain, while energy was the weakest sector as oil fell.

items.headline: Fed meeting under way; decision lands early Thursday Singapore time
items.summary: Most investors expect the Fed to hold rates. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 5%. Alphabet and Microsoft report after Wednesday's close, with AI spending the key question.

items.headline: Oil drops almost $2 on Middle East peace talks
items.summary: Brent settled at $113.88 and WTI at $99.90 as Iran held talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan. Prices remain near six-month highs: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue and October was the worst month for shipping attacks around Hormuz since tracking began in 2017. UBS now sees Brent near $110 to year-end.

items.headline: Boeing sinks 10.7% after missing 737 targets
items.summary: CEO Kelly Ortberg said Boeing will miss this year's 737 production and delivery goals, and pushed back its cash-flow outlook to about $3bn next year, well below the $5.5bn analysts expected. It was the stock's worst day in more than 18 months.

items.headline: HSBC slides about 6% despite 32% profit jump
items.summary: Third-quarter pre-tax profit of $9.6bn met forecasts, but revenue of $18.6bn missed and wealth income stalled after two strong quarters. The bank announced another buyback of up to $1bn.

items.headline: Germany's Merz makes first official visit; new Joint Work Plan unveiled
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz is in Singapore from 27 to 28 October. The two governments launched a Joint Work Plan for the next stage of relations, and Merz said he would like Germany to learn from Singapore's National Service.

items.headline: Singapore and Indonesia to form joint haze task force
items.summary: The task force will share data and investigate companies linked to the forest fires. Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan was in Jakarta to meet his Indonesian counterpart amid strained ties over the haze.

items.headline: Indonesia gas cut is under 2% of Singapore's demand, EMA says
items.summary: Jakarta cut piped gas to Singapore by 31 BBTUD from 24 October, citing domestic needs, days after a minister warned of curbs on countries that did not 'respect' Indonesia. It says the cut is within contract limits; the Energy Market Authority says supply remains adequate.

items.headline: Woman pleads guilty in Megan Khung abuse case
items.summary: A Singaporean woman admitted conspiring to abuse four-year-old Megan Khung and helping dispose of her body.
items.source: The Straits Times; South China Morning Post

items.headline: Sisters' Islands Marine Park named Singapore's first 'Hope Spot'
items.summary: The marine park has received the international ocean-conservation designation, recognising it as an area critical to marine health.

items.headline: Haze row deepens between Indonesia and its neighbours
items.summary: President Prabowo has hit back at countries that 'insult' Indonesia, while Malaysia says it will raise the haze at an ASEAN meeting in Manila. Singapore has served legal notices on 10 Indonesian firms it suspects of causing fires.

items.headline: Indonesia scouts sites for its first nuclear power plant
items.summary: Officials are assessing locations including the Riau Islands and Halmahera as part of a long-term energy-security push, and separately offered 43 oil and gas discoveries to investors.

items.headline: Thailand weighs fuel-tax cuts as Chinese EV imports surge
items.summary: Cabinet is considering excise cuts on E20 petrol and B20 diesel plus subsidies for home solar. Car imports more than doubled in September, driven by electric vehicles, almost all from China.

items.headline: Malaysia and Thailand push closer border and economic links
items.summary: Two high-level meetings in Bangkok focused on border connectivity, security cooperation and trade.

items.headline: ASEAN defence talks open in the Philippines without China's minister
items.summary: Chinese Defence Minister Dong Jun will miss the meetings as Beijing's party plenum convenes. The US and South Korean defence chiefs plan talks on the sidelines.

items.headline: Nikkei snaps three-day slide on AI optimism
items.summary: The index rose 1.7% to 63,268 as Anthropic's IPO filing revived appetite for AI stocks; Advantest jumped 9.6% and SoftBank Group 5%. The Nikkei is still about 14% below its June record.

items.headline: Xi mourns ex-PM Fukuda, urges Tokyo to protect ties
items.summary: Former prime minister Yasuo Fukuda died on Thursday aged 90. In a rare direct comment on strained relations, Xi Jinping urged Japan's current leaders to 'safeguard the political foundation' of ties, which soured after PM Takaichi's Taiwan remarks last November.

items.headline: Government holds urgent cybersecurity meeting after breach wave
items.summary: More than 20 major companies have disclosed attacks since September, from Times Car to JR East via a ransomware hit on a SoftBank cloud unit. Takaichi said Japan would act 'strategically' and keep active cyber defence on the table.

items.headline: Criteria set for a backup 'secondary capital'
items.summary: Cabinet approved rules for designating a second capital in case of a major Kanto disaster. Only Hokkaido, Aichi, Osaka and Fukuoka qualify, and all four are preparing bids.

items.headline: Keen Sword drills deploy long-range missiles off base for first time
items.summary: The Japan-US exercise, running to 29 October with about 45,000 Japanese and 12,000 US personnel, moved Japan's 1,000km-range Type 25 anti-ship missiles to a Kyushu training ground. No live firing is planned.

items.headline: Economy grows 3.4% on AI chip boom, far beating forecasts
items.summary: Third-quarter GDP rose 1.0% on the quarter against the central bank's 0.3% forecast, driven by chip exports and investment. Private consumption fell 0.2%.

items.headline: Bank of Korea warns chip exports could drop by up to $100bn
items.summary: In a pessimistic scenario where US tech giants curb AI spending next year, semiconductor exports could fall $50–100bn below earlier forecasts.

items.headline: Kospi jumps 3.1% ahead of chipmaker results
items.summary: The index closed at 5,638 after SK Hynix and Samsung surged. SK Hynix reports today and Samsung on Thursday; Samsung has guided for an almost eight-fold rise in operating profit.

items.headline: Lee presses on with Pacific trade pact bid
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung said Korea must pursue CPTPP membership despite opposition, pledging compensation for affected farmers.

items.headline: Lee says Europe's unrest is a warning about low growth
items.summary: At a Cabinet meeting, Lee said sluggish growth, more than living costs or inequality, lies at the root of protests across Europe, and Korea must learn from it.

items.headline: Inflation data due at 8:30am Singapore time could seal a rate hike
items.summary: The big four banks expect core (trimmed mean) inflation of about 1.0% for the September quarter, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast, with fuel driving headline prices. The cash rate is 4.60% after four hikes this year; the RBA meets on 3 November.

items.headline: Albanese concedes he misled parliament over golf club grant
items.summary: The PM admitted giving incorrect information about a $6m grant to Marrickville Golf Club in his electorate, after officials rejected his claim it was partly for sewerage works.

items.headline: Government defends migration overhaul
items.summary: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke set out changes to the migration system; Albanese said net overseas migration is down 45% and he will raise the influx of UK backpackers with British PM Andy Burnham.

items.headline: Defence buying to move to an independent agency
items.summary: After years of blowouts and delays, procurement will shift to a new Defence Delivery Agency from July 2027, led by a former mining executive.

items.headline: New defence framework with Timor-Leste
items.summary: Deputy PM Richard Marles called Timor-Leste a critical link in Australia's regional security network, completing a push to deepen ties across the Pacific and Southeast Asia.

items.headline: One week to midterms; Democrats hold slight edge
items.summary: An NPR/PBS News/Marist poll shows Democrats narrowly ahead before the 3 November vote, with both parties focusing on living costs.

items.headline: Trump says he will respect results 'if they're honest'
items.summary: The president again declined to commit unconditionally to accepting the midterm outcome while campaigning in Texas and Mississippi.

items.headline: Grand jury declines to indict Cassidy Hutchinson
items.summary: The refusal to charge the former White House aide is the latest setback for the Justice Department's efforts, AP sources said.

items.headline: Judge halts DC golf course renovation
items.summary: A federal judge barred more tree clearing at East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says work will still begin next month and the administration will appeal.

items.headline: Pentagon labels Confucius Institutes a security threat
items.summary: The Defense Department designated the Chinese-funded campus centres a national-security threat; Beijing condemned the 'smearing and stigmatisation'.

items.headline: Party plenum focuses on discipline and loyalty ahead of 2027 congress
items.summary: The four-day fifth plenum, ending Thursday with a communique, centres on 'full and rigorous party self-governance'. Analysts see it as the last major gathering before the 2027 reshuffle, where Xi is expected to secure a fourth term.

items.headline: Industrial profits up 14.4%, fastest since June
items.summary: AI-linked electronics and pricier commodities drove the September jump (from 4.2% in August); profits are up 15.5% so far this year. Consumer-facing sectors continue to lag on weak demand.

items.headline: China's AI stock bubble has already burst
items.summary: The STAR 50 index of AI and chip leaders has fallen about 40% in under four months, wiping out around $480bn. The CSI 300 sank deeper into a bear market, down 1.3% on Tuesday.

items.headline: Taiwan rebuffs Beijing's 'Restoration Day' commemorations
items.summary: China marked the anniversary of Japan's 1945 handover of Taiwan with satellite images of Taipei landmarks and a military poster; Taiwan's defence minister called it 'cognitive warfare'.

items.headline: Defence minister Dong Jun skips ASEAN talks
items.summary: China's defence chief will miss the regional defence meetings in the Philippines while the plenum is in session.

items.headline: 'Very severe' Cyclone Arnab makes landfall this morning
items.summary: The storm is due to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by late morning with winds of 115–125 km/h. Around 400,000 people need evacuating and dozens of train services are suspended.

items.headline: Rupee stuck near 95 per dollar despite heavy RBI support
items.summary: The central bank has spent about $80bn defending the currency since June as oil and foreign outflows weigh. Former governor Raghuram Rajan said India should not 'fixate on a number'.

items.headline: Stocks flat as oil and the Fed weigh
items.summary: The Sensex closed at 73,598.67 and the Nifty at 22,749.75, both barely changed, amid continued foreign selling.

items.headline: Modi urges India to lead in future tech, warns on blind trust in AI
items.summary: Opening a three-day science and innovation conclave in New Delhi, the PM called for indigenous capability in AI, biotech, energy and other critical technologies.

items.headline: BRICS parliamentary forum condemns unilateral sanctions
items.summary: Lawmakers from BRICS countries meeting in New Delhi issued a joint stance against sanctions imposed outside multilateral frameworks.
